title: Roast my trailer (I need feedback)
author: Embarrassed_Text_347
selftext:
Ok so I'm working on this trailer and I feel like it's currently like a 6/10 but I don't really know where or how to improve it. Would it be better to go full AI? I know a lot of mobile games tend to have AI trailers, but I don't really know where I would start.

The game is about cleaning up lakes and you upgrade your boat, get better gear, etc.

Here's the store links for more info:  
Android: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.gubestudios.cleanwake](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.gubestudios.cleanwake)  
iOS: [https://apps.apple.com/us/app/clean-wake-water-cleanup-game/id6832360665](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/clean-wake-water-cleanup-game/id6832360665)

I haven't posted the trailer yet because I wanted some feedback to see where it can be better. Would AI generated be a decent route to go? Or does the trailer just need to be improved?

comments.author: boynet2
comments.body: maybe try to show some mor? maybe when it say upgrade your boat, show some upgrade menu and click on the upgrade

replies.author: Embarrassed_Text_347
replies.body: True yeah I could show the upgrades menu.

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/Embarrassed_Text_347 please add some details about how you used AI to develop this. Saying you used AI isn't enough on its own. We're looking for the actual dev details. Rule 4 asks promotional posts to contribute by talking about the process and the actual development. We're trying to keep the sub from filling up with low quality game posts. If this doesn't get updated, it may be removed.

comments.author: BobertS42
comments.body: This looks like almost every mobile game add now adays.

replies.author: MrJurasek
replies.body: Which is actually a good thing -> those ads usually bring low cost per install. So if this game would actually deliver what the trailer promises, it would be a nice refreshment among the sea full of fake ads promising gameplay that doesn't exist.

replies.author: Embarrassed_Text_347
replies.body: Currently I'm just using the store screenshots for paid ads and I'm around $1 CPI (for US-based), but you think this trailer would have better metrics? I'm glad you like that it's realistic. I'm just worried it won't be "appealing" enough compared to the other mobile ads that are out there.

replies.author: MrJurasek
replies.body:
I don't know on which platform you run ads and what is your setup, but I would definitely try some videos in the mix as well. Alternatively if you are looking for creative winners, you can test it out on cheaper markets and then use creative winners on US, since US is one of the most expensive ones. 

I can imagine that AI can generate you tons of videos with various scenarios and hooks that you can quickly test out

replies.author: Embarrassed_Text_347
replies.body:
Good point about the cheap testing. I wanted to test US first because I didn't want to just flood my app with cheap installs, but using it to gauge an ad is a smart idea.

I have used chatgpt to talk through some scenarios but it's hard to find a super strong hook for a casual cleanup game 😂. I will just have to test a bunch of variations I suppose.

comments.author: No_Actuator_1353
comments.body: the trailer is indeed a bit slow but I like the game!

replies.author: Embarrassed_Text_347
replies.body: Thanks! How would you suggest improving it? Is it the footage not being cut fast enough, actual speed of gameplay? I could just put the whole thing in 1.25x speed 😂.

comments.author: modern12
comments.body: Your game seems to be built around sucking in stuff, so put your effort into making sucking as satisfying and pleasant as possible.

comments.author: PoleTree
comments.body:
I'll give some feedback on the trailer and the game.


Trailer

* boring text and text animations. text always in the same place.
* music is alright, I think something a little more upbeat and/or cheerful/whimsical might fit the cozy restoration vibe more?
* camera is always looking at the same thing (boat from the same height/angle). Maybe add some nice UI shots or different camera angles if you have any that would work in a trailer.
* Final dirty/clean transition is not exciting (all garbage just disappears). maybe have like a quickly expanding circle from the middle of the video (outside=dirty, inside=clean) or a slanted line move across the screen to show the contrast more? Maybe some sparkle effects to denote the cleanliness?
* Music just cuts off at the end, no outro transition.
* Someone already suggested more focus on the upgrades. Maybe zoom the camera in and show the upgrades being applied to the boat (if you have an animation for that) or a quick set of images showing different upgrade states/configurations.



Game

* the garbage collection sound is kinda annoying
* returning garbage is not exciting/engaging enough (although you didn't show the whole process so maybe it is). There should be some sort of visual/audio exclamation when you unload all the garbage that makes you feel good. I would show that in the trailer too.
* the boat's water effects needs some work (better wave/wake visuals, etc)
* oil spill looks weird after cleanup, just a straight line cut through it.
* collected garbage visuals are a little plain (stacked garbage bags). maybe add different types of garbage or have it be more of a disorganized pile instead of straight columns?

Looks pretty good so far though

replies.author: Embarrassed_Text_347
replies.body: Thanks for all of this! I'll definitely work on improving some of these aspects.

comments.author: homezlice
comments.body: "Full load" is maybe a better name than "Clean Wake"?

comments.author: OkVariety8064
comments.body:
It looks like an early prototype level clone of [Spilled!](https://store.steampowered.com/app/2240080/Spilled/) which itself was a clone of some older game I forgot.

The key question would be how to differentiate yourself from those other games with the same basic idea. As for how to make the world feel living and consistent, just look at a close enough level how Spilled! uses colours, shapes and so on to communicate different aspects of the world.

replies.author: Embarrassed_Text_347
replies.body: Cool! I actually looked around and couldn't find any other games like this (except a very bad mobile game). Had no clue there was a steam game already. The steam game looks really good.
